goal: Allow local RPC and REST traffic over UNIX domain sockets instead of TCP loopback
Let node operators use filesystem permissions rather than IP allowlists to control local RPC access
Reduce overhead and clean up networking abstractions tangled with P2P classes
agreement: Broad concept support for long-sought UNIX socket support (winterrdog, b-l-u-e, vasild)
Approach approved for socket abstraction design and security (winterrdog)
Unaddressed objection: tests hang on FreeBSD due to wake-up behavior on closed sockets (winterrdog)
Unaddressed objection: NetBSD test fails with buffer space OSError due to buffer size limits (winterrdog)

categories.name: rpc
why: P2 because it fulfills a decade-old feature request for UNIX domain sockets in JSON-RPC and REST
Allows local operators to replace TCP loopback allowlists with standard OS filesystem permissions
Removes TCP overhead for local tooling and resolves isolated technical debt from prior socket work
